label: Howard et al. confidence sequences over unbounded horizons
summary: Howard et al. report constructing shrinking confidence sequences with time-uniform, nonasymptotic coverage under nonparametric conditions.

label: Vovk and Wang e-value averaging
summary: Vovk and Wang report that multiple e-values for one hypothesis can be merged by averaging them.

label: Xu and Ramdas e-LOND dependence-robust online FDR
summary: Xu and Ramdas report e-LOND control of online false discovery rate under arbitrary, possibly unknown, dependence.

label: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas bounded-mean betting inference
summary: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas report martingale-based confidence intervals and time-uniform sequences for bounded means, including sampling without replacement and adaptation to unknown variance.

sources.title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting

label: Choe and Ramdas filtration-mismatch warning
summary: Choe and Ramdas report that e-process validity in a coarser filtration does not automatically hold in a finer filtration, preventing unadjusted averaging across them.

label: Choe and Ramdas adjust-then-combine procedure
summary: Choe and Ramdas report an adjust-then-combine procedure lifting e-processes across filtrations, with a logarithmic validity-recovery cost.

label: Dwork et al. reusable holdout for adaptive validation
summary: Dwork et al. report that adaptive holdout reuse risks overfitting and propose an algorithm to validate many adaptively chosen hypotheses while avoiding that overfitting.

sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse

label: Lee et al. selection-conditional inference for lasso
summary: Lee et al. report selection-conditional inference for lasso-selected coefficients, including confidence intervals and tests.

sources.title: Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso

label: Ramdas et al. necessity of martingales for admissible anytime-valid inference
summary: Ramdas et al. report that all admissible confidence sequences, p-processes and e-processes rely on nonnegative martingales under their formal admissibility definition.

sources.title: Admissible anytime-valid sequential inference must rely on nonnegative martingales
